title: Scheduled price changes
scenario: A Diwali price set for midnight went live at noon, and two overlapping prices made checkout pick one at random.
stack: Spring Boot 4.1.1 · Java 25 · JdbcClient · effective dating · timestamptz and time zones · PostgreSQL 17 EXCLUDE with tstzrange · Testcontainers

Level 1, about 5 minutes. Plain language: no code.

The problem in real life

  1. Diwali pricing

    A seller sets Rangoli Colours to Rs 149 from midnight on 8 November.

  2. Noon, not midnight

    A job checked for due price changes twice a day and overwrote the price when it ran: the sale went live at noon. The times had no time zone either, so a server on UTC read "midnight" as 05:30 in India. And when a flash sale was added inside the Diwali sale, both applied, and checkout took whichever the database returned first.

  3. The fix

    Store every price with its window as instants. "The price now" is just the window containing now: nothing has to run at midnight. The database refuses two windows that overlap.

Do not change data at a scheduled time. Store data that is valid from a time, and read it as of now.

What are we building?

POST /products/2/prices schedules a price for a window; GET /products/2/price?at=… answers the price at any instant, past or future.

An everyday analogy

A railway timetable. Nobody repaints the board at midnight to show tomorrow's trains; the timetable lists each train with its days, and you read the line for today. Two trains on one platform at the same time cannot both be printed.

How it works in 4 steps

  1. Read the seller's local times in the shop's zone, India, and turn them into instants.
  2. Make room: windows inside the new one go, the one covering its start is cut there, and the old price resumes after it.
  3. Insert the new window. The database checks nothing overlaps.
  4. Answer "price at" with the one window containing that instant.
Check yourself: the sale ends "at midnight on 11 November". What does a customer pay at exactly 00:00:00 that night?

The normal price. Windows are half-open: the sale includes its start and excludes its end, so at midnight the next window has begun. The test checks both edges.

What this station is not

  • No checkout. Freezing the price on an order line is Practice 3.
  • No currencies or taxes. One price in paise.
  • No several shop zones. One zone, set in configuration.

Level 2. What a teammate hands you before you build.

Business problem

Kartwala (a fictional marketplace): a Diwali price set for midnight went live at noon, and two overlapping prices made checkout pick one at random.

Acceptance criteria

Demo data: Rangoli Colours is Rs 199, Rs 149 from midnight 8 November to midnight 11 November, then Rs 199 again. Tests fix "now" at 16 October 2026, 11:30 in India.

  1. Given 23:59:59 on 7 November in India, then Rs 199; at 00:00:00 on 8 November, Rs 149, asked in IST or in UTC.
  2. Given 00:00 on 11 November, then Rs 199 again.
  3. Given a past instant, then the price that was valid then.
  4. Given a sale inside the base price, then three windows: base, sale, base.
  5. Given a change in the past, then 422; an end before the start, 400; an unknown product, 404.
  6. Given an overlapping window written directly, then the database refuses it.

Requirements

  • Prices are never overwritten; each has a window.
  • Windows are half-open and stored as instants (timestamptz).
  • Seller times are read in the shop's zone; questions may use any offset.
  • At most one price per product at any instant, enforced by the database.
  • One schedule change per product at a time.

Learning objectives

  • Model effective-dated data with half-open windows.
  • Write "as of" queries.
  • Handle local times, zones and instants without surprises.
  • Enforce "no overlap" with an exclusion constraint.

The trap

Plausible but wrong

Overwriting the price at a scheduled time instead of storing dated prices.

The old design kept one current price and a table of planned changes with timestamp (no zone) and no rule against overlaps. A job applied them when it ran, and lost each old price as it did. The test recreates the planned-changes table and reads it as the UTC server did:

  • Midnight in the wrong place. At 00:30 in India on 8 November, the old query finds no sale; at 05:30 in India (midnight UTC) it does. The new API answers Rs 149 at 00:30.
  • Two prices at once. A flash sale added inside the Diwali sale: at noon on the 9th, both rows match. Checkout's LIMIT 1 took one; which, depended on the plan.
  • The real table refuses the overlap: prices_no_overlap.

While building, each fix was undone once: reading seller times as UTC turned 3 tests red; dropping the exclusion constraint 3; not resuming the old price after a window 2; a closed end (valid_to >= at) 1; not shifting a window that starts inside 1; no past check 1.

package com.kartwala.prices;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.catchThrowable;

/**
 * Written first. The old schedule table: local times without a time zone, no rule against overlaps, read by a server
 * whose clock runs in UTC.
 */
class OverwrittenPriceTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    /** The old checkout query: the price change in force "now", as the UTC server's local time saw it. */
    static final String OLD = """
            SELECT price_paise FROM old_price_changes WHERE product_id = 2
            AND starts_at <= (CAST(:at AS timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND ends_at > (CAST(:at AS timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')""";

    @BeforeEach
    void oldTable() {
        jdbc.sql("CREATE TABLE old_price_changes (product_id BIGINT, price_paise INTEGER, starts_at TIMESTAMP, ends_at TIMESTAMP)").update();
        // The seller typed midnight, meaning midnight in India.
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO old_price_changes VALUES (2, 14900, '2026-11-08 00:00', '2026-11-11 00:00')").update();
    }

    @AfterEach
    void dropOldTable() {
        jdbc.sql("DROP TABLE old_price_changes").update();
    }

    private List<Integer> old(String at) {
        return jdbc.sql(OLD).param("at", at).query(Integer.class).list();
    }

    @Test
    void localTimesWentLiveAtTheServersMidnightNotTheShops() throws Exception {
        assertThat(old("2026-11-08T00:30:00+05:30")).isEmpty();                 // half an hour into Diwali in India: no sale yet
        assertThat(old("2026-11-08T05:30:00+05:30")).containsExactly(14900);    // midnight in UTC
        priceAt(2, "2026-11-08T00:30:00+05:30").andExpect(org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath("$.pricePaise").value(14900));
    }

    @Test
    void twoOverlappingChangesBothApplyAndCheckoutPicksOne() {
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO old_price_changes VALUES (2, 12900, '2026-11-09 00:00', '2026-11-10 00:00')").update();   // a flash sale, added later
        assertThat(old("2026-11-09T12:00:00+05:30")).containsExactlyInAnyOrder(14900, 12900);   // which one checkout took depended on the plan
    }

    @Test
    void theRealTableRefusesTheOverlap() {
        Throwable refused = catchThrowable(() -> jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO prices (product_id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to) VALUES (2, 12900, '2026-11-09 00:00+05:30', '2026-11-10 00:00+05:30')").update());
        assertThat(refused).hasMessageContaining("prices_no_overlap");
    }
}

Without it

package com.kartwala.prices;

import jakarta.validation.Valid;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Max;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.Min;
import jakarta.validation.constraints.NotNull;
import org.springframework.format.annotation.DateTimeFormat;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PostMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestBody;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.ResponseStatus;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;

@RestController
class PriceController {

    /** Times are the shop's local time, as a seller types them: "2026-11-08T00:00" means midnight in India. */
    record NewPrice(@NotNull @Min(100) @Max(10_000_000) Integer pricePaise, @NotNull LocalDateTime from, LocalDateTime to) {
    }

    private final PriceSchedule schedule;
    private final Clock clock;

    PriceController(PriceSchedule schedule, Clock clock) {
        this.schedule = schedule;
        this.clock = clock;
    }

    @PostMapping("/products/{id}/prices")
    @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED)
    PriceSchedule.Schedule set(@PathVariable long id, @Valid @RequestBody NewPrice body) {
        return schedule.set(id, body.pricePaise(), body.from(), body.to());
    }

    /** ?at=2026-11-08T00:30+05:30 (an instant, with its offset); now when absent. */
    @GetMapping("/products/{id}/price")
    PriceSchedule.PriceAt price(@PathVariable long id, @RequestParam(required = false) @DateTimeFormat(iso = DateTimeFormat.ISO.DATE_TIME) OffsetDateTime at) {
        return schedule.priceAt(id, at == null ? clock.instant() : at.toInstant());
    }
}

src/main/java/com/kartwala/prices/PriceSchedule.java

Does
Answers "price at" and fits a new window into the schedule.
Why
One transaction, the product row locked, neighbours trimmed or continued, then the insert.
Without it
Overlaps refused by the database instead of fitted, or prices overwritten.
  • Instants are bound as OffsetDateTime in UTC: the database session's zone never matters.
  • The shop zone comes from shop.zone, and Clock is a bean so tests fix "now".
package com.kartwala.prices;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;

/** Dated prices: a new price never overwrites; it takes its stretch of time, and the neighbours give way. */
@Service
class PriceSchedule {

    record Window(int pricePaise, OffsetDateTime from, OffsetDateTime to) {
    }

    record Schedule(long productId, List<Window> windows) {
    }

    record PriceAt(long productId, OffsetDateTime at, int pricePaise, OffsetDateTime validFrom, OffsetDateTime validTo) {
    }

    private record Row(long id, int pricePaise, Instant validFrom, Instant validTo) {
    }

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;
    private final Clock clock;
    private final ZoneId zone;

    PriceSchedule(JdbcClient jdbc, Clock clock, @Value("${shop.zone}") ZoneId zone) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.clock = clock;
        this.zone = zone;
    }

    /** The one price valid at that instant: valid_from <= at < valid_to. The exclusion constraint makes "one" true. */
    PriceAt priceAt(long productId, Instant at) {
        requireProduct(productId);
        return jdbc.sql("""
                        SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices
                        WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from <= ? AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > ?)""")
                .params(productId, utc(at), utc(at)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional()
                .map(r -> new PriceAt(productId, local(at), r.pricePaise(), local(r.validFrom()), local(r.validTo())))
                .orElseThrow(() -> new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Product " + productId + " has no price at " + local(at)));
    }

    /**
     * Sets a price for [from, to) in shop time; to null means "from then on". Rows inside the window go, a row
     * covering its start is cut there, and a row covering its end continues after it.
     */
    @Transactional
    Schedule set(long productId, int pricePaise, LocalDateTime fromLocal, LocalDateTime toLocal) {
        Instant from = fromLocal.atZone(zone).toInstant();
        Instant to = toLocal == null ? null : toLocal.atZone(zone).toInstant();
        if (to != null && !to.isAfter(from)) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "The price must end after it starts");
        }
        if (from.isBefore(clock.instant())) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Prices in the past are history and cannot change");
        }
        // One schedule change per product at a time: a second one waits here, then sees the first one's rows.
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT id FROM products WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE").param(productId).query(Long.class).optional().isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No product " + productId);
        }
        Optional<Row> covering = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from < ? AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > ?)")
                .params(productId, utc(from), utc(from)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional();
        if (to == null) {
            jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ?").params(productId, utc(from)).update();
        } else {
            jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ? AND valid_to IS NOT NULL AND valid_to <= ?").params(productId, utc(from), utc(to)).update();
            jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_from = ? WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ? AND valid_from < ?").params(utc(to), productId, utc(from), utc(to)).update();
        }
        covering.ifPresent(c -> {
            jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_to = ? WHERE id = ?").params(utc(from), c.id()).update();
            if (to != null && (c.validTo() == null || c.validTo().isAfter(to))) {   // the old price resumes after the new window
                insert(productId, c.pricePaise(), to, c.validTo());
            }
        });
        try {
            insert(productId, pricePaise, from, to);
        } catch (DataIntegrityViolationException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "The schedule changed meanwhile; read it and try again");
        }
        return schedule(productId);
    }

    Schedule schedule(long productId) {
        List<Window> windows = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? ORDER BY valid_from")
                .param(productId).query(PriceSchedule::row).list().stream()
                .map(r -> new Window(r.pricePaise(), local(r.validFrom()), local(r.validTo()))).toList();
        return new Schedule(productId, windows);
    }

    private void insert(long productId, int pricePaise, Instant from, Instant to) {
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO prices (product_id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)")
                .params(productId, pricePaise, utc(from), utc(to)).update();
    }

    private void requireProduct(long productId) {
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE id = ?").param(productId).query(Long.class).single() == 0) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No product " + productId);
        }
    }

    private OffsetDateTime local(Instant instant) {
        return instant == null ? null : instant.atZone(zone).toOffsetDateTime();
    }

    /** Bound as an offset date-time, so PostgreSQL never interprets it in the server's or session's time zone. */
    private static OffsetDateTime utc(Instant instant) {
        return instant == null ? null : instant.atOffset(ZoneOffset.UTC);
    }

    private static Row row(java.sql.ResultSet rs, int i) throws java.sql.SQLException {
        OffsetDateTime to = rs.getObject("valid_to", OffsetDateTime.class);
        return new Row(rs.getLong("id"), rs.getInt("price_paise"), rs.getObject("valid_from", OffsetDateTime.class).toInstant(), to == null ? null : to.toInstant());
    }
}

Why

Without it
Two matching rows, and a checkout that picks one.
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist;   -- lets a GiST exclusion constraint compare product_id with =

CREATE TABLE products (
    id   BIGINT       PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);

-- Every price a product has had or will have, each valid for a half-open stretch of time [valid_from, valid_to).
-- valid_to NULL means "until further notice". Nothing is overwritten, so "what did it cost at 21:04 yesterday" has an answer.
CREATE TABLE prices (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id  BIGINT      NOT NULL CONSTRAINT prices_product_fk REFERENCES products (id),
    price_paise INTEGER     NOT NULL CONSTRAINT prices_price_range CHECK (price_paise BETWEEN 100 AND 10000000),
    valid_from  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    valid_to    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    CONSTRAINT prices_window_order CHECK (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > valid_from),

    CONSTRAINT prices_no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (product_id WITH =, tstzrange(valid_from, valid_to, '[)') WITH &&)

package com.kartwala.prices;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.AfterEach;
import org.junit.jupiter.api.BeforeEach;

import java.util.List;

import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.assertThat;
import static org.assertj.core.api.Assertions.catchThrowable;

/**
 * Written first. The old schedule table: local times without a time zone, no rule against overlaps, read by a server
 * whose clock runs in UTC.
 */
class OverwrittenPriceTrapTest extends ApiTest {

    /** The old checkout query: the price change in force "now", as the UTC server's local time saw it. */
    static final String OLD = """
            SELECT price_paise FROM old_price_changes WHERE product_id = 2
            AND starts_at <= (CAST(:at AS timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AND ends_at > (CAST(:at AS timestamptz) AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')""";

    @BeforeEach
    void oldTable() {
        jdbc.sql("CREATE TABLE old_price_changes (product_id BIGINT, price_paise INTEGER, starts_at TIMESTAMP, ends_at TIMESTAMP)").update();
        // The seller typed midnight, meaning midnight in India.
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO old_price_changes VALUES (2, 14900, '2026-11-08 00:00', '2026-11-11 00:00')").update();
    }

    @AfterEach
    void dropOldTable() {
        jdbc.sql("DROP TABLE old_price_changes").update();
    }

    private List<Integer> old(String at) {
        return jdbc.sql(OLD).param("at", at).query(Integer.class).list();
    }

    @Test
    void localTimesWentLiveAtTheServersMidnightNotTheShops() throws Exception {
        assertThat(old("2026-11-08T00:30:00+05:30")).isEmpty();                 // half an hour into Diwali in India: no sale yet
        assertThat(old("2026-11-08T05:30:00+05:30")).containsExactly(14900);    // midnight in UTC
        priceAt(2, "2026-11-08T00:30:00+05:30").andExpect(org.springframework.test.web.servlet.result.MockMvcResultMatchers.jsonPath("$.pricePaise").value(14900));
    }

    @Test
    void twoOverlappingChangesBothApplyAndCheckoutPicksOne() {
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO old_price_changes VALUES (2, 12900, '2026-11-09 00:00', '2026-11-10 00:00')").update();   // a flash sale, added later
        assertThat(old("2026-11-09T12:00:00+05:30")).containsExactlyInAnyOrder(14900, 12900);   // which one checkout took depended on the plan
    }

    @Test
    void theRealTableRefusesTheOverlap() {
        Throwable refused = catchThrowable(() -> jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO prices (product_id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to) VALUES (2, 12900, '2026-11-09 00:00+05:30', '2026-11-10 00:00+05:30')").update());
        assertThat(refused).hasMessageContaining("prices_no_overlap");
    }
}

        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO prices (product_id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to) VALUES (?, ?, CAST(? AS timestamptz), CAST(? AS timestamptz))")
                .params(product, paise, from, to).update();

                .hasMessageContaining("prices_no_overlap");   // product 1's base price is open-ended
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> price(9, 49900, "2027-01-01 00:00+05:30", null)).hasMessageContaining("prices_product_fk");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> price(3, 0, "2025-01-01 00:00+05:30", "2025-02-01 00:00+05:30")).hasMessageContaining("prices_price_range");
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> price(3, 9900, "2025-02-01 00:00+05:30", "2025-01-01 00:00+05:30")).hasMessageContaining("prices_window_order");
    }

    @Test
    void aWindowMayStartExactlyWhereAnotherEnds() {
        price(3, 79900, "2025-01-01 00:00+05:30", "2026-01-01 00:00+05:30");   // ends where the first 2026 price begins: half-open, no overlap
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM prices WHERE product_id = 3").query(Long.class).single()).isEqualTo(3);
    }

    @Test
    void aBatchWithOneOverlapAddsNothing() {
        assertThatThrownBy(() -> transaction.executeWithoutResult(tx -> {
            price(3, 79900, "2025-01-01 00:00+05:30", "2025-06-01 00:00+05:30");
            price(3, 69900, "2025-05-01 00:00+05:30", "2025-07-01 00:00+05:30");
        })).hasMessageContaining("prices_no_overlap");
        assertThat(jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM prices WHERE product_id = 3").query(Long.class).single()).isEqualTo(2);
    }
}

package com.kartwala.prices;

import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException;
import org.springframework.http.HttpStatus;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient;
import org.springframework.stereotype.Service;
import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;

/** Dated prices: a new price never overwrites; it takes its stretch of time, and the neighbours give way. */
@Service
class PriceSchedule {

    record Window(int pricePaise, OffsetDateTime from, OffsetDateTime to) {
    }

    record Schedule(long productId, List<Window> windows) {
    }

    record PriceAt(long productId, OffsetDateTime at, int pricePaise, OffsetDateTime validFrom, OffsetDateTime validTo) {
    }

    private record Row(long id, int pricePaise, Instant validFrom, Instant validTo) {
    }

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;
    private final Clock clock;
    private final ZoneId zone;

    PriceSchedule(JdbcClient jdbc, Clock clock, @Value("${shop.zone}") ZoneId zone) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.clock = clock;
        this.zone = zone;
    }

    /** The one price valid at that instant: valid_from <= at < valid_to. The exclusion constraint makes "one" true. */
    PriceAt priceAt(long productId, Instant at) {
        requireProduct(productId);
        return jdbc.sql("""
                        SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices
                        WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from <= ? AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > ?)""")
                .params(productId, utc(at), utc(at)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional()
                .map(r -> new PriceAt(productId, local(at), r.pricePaise(), local(r.validFrom()), local(r.validTo())))
                .orElseThrow(() -> new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Product " + productId + " has no price at " + local(at)));
    }

    /**
     * Sets a price for [from, to) in shop time; to null means "from then on". Rows inside the window go, a row
     * covering its start is cut there, and a row covering its end continues after it.
     */
    @Transactional
    Schedule set(long productId, int pricePaise, LocalDateTime fromLocal, LocalDateTime toLocal) {
        Instant from = fromLocal.atZone(zone).toInstant();
        Instant to = toLocal == null ? null : toLocal.atZone(zone).toInstant();
        if (to != null && !to.isAfter(from)) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "The price must end after it starts");
        }
        if (from.isBefore(clock.instant())) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Prices in the past are history and cannot change");
        }
        // One schedule change per product at a time: a second one waits here, then sees the first one's rows.
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT id FROM products WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE").param(productId).query(Long.class).optional().isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No product " + productId);
        }
        Optional<Row> covering = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from < ? AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > ?)")
                .params(productId, utc(from), utc(from)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional();
        if (to == null) {
            jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ?").params(productId, utc(from)).update();
        } else {
            jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ? AND valid_to IS NOT NULL AND valid_to <= ?").params(productId, utc(from), utc(to)).update();
            jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_from = ? WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ? AND valid_from < ?").params(utc(to), productId, utc(from), utc(to)).update();
        }
        covering.ifPresent(c -> {
            jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_to = ? WHERE id = ?").params(utc(from), c.id()).update();
            if (to != null && (c.validTo() == null || c.validTo().isAfter(to))) {   // the old price resumes after the new window
                insert(productId, c.pricePaise(), to, c.validTo());
            }
        });
        try {
            insert(productId, pricePaise, from, to);
        } catch (DataIntegrityViolationException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "The schedule changed meanwhile; read it and try again");
        }
        return schedule(productId);
    }

    /** Challenge 1. */
    Schedule fullSchedule(long productId) {
        requireProduct(productId);
        return schedule(productId);
    }

    /** Challenge 2: remove one future window; the window before it stretches over the gap, and equal neighbours merge. */
    @Transactional
    Schedule cancel(long productId, LocalDateTime fromLocal) {
        Instant from = fromLocal.atZone(zone).toInstant();
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT id FROM products WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE").param(productId).query(Long.class).optional().isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No product " + productId);
        }
        Row window = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from = ?")
                .params(productId, utc(from)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No price starts at " + fromLocal));
        if (!window.validFrom().isAfter(clock.instant())) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Prices in the past are history and cannot change");
        }
        jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE id = ?").param(window.id()).update();
        Optional<Row> before = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_to = ?")
                .params(productId, utc(from)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional();
        Optional<Row> after = window.validTo() == null ? Optional.empty()
                : jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from = ?")
                        .params(productId, utc(window.validTo())).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional();
        before.ifPresent(b -> {
            if (after.isPresent() && after.get().pricePaise() == b.pricePaise()) {   // same price on both sides: one window
                jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE id = ?").param(after.get().id()).update();
                jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_to = ? WHERE id = ?").params(utc(after.get().validTo()), b.id()).update();
            } else {
                jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_to = ? WHERE id = ?").params(utc(window.validTo()), b.id()).update();
            }
        });
        return schedule(productId);
    }

                .param(productId).query(PriceSchedule::row).list().stream()
                .map(r -> new Window(r.pricePaise(), local(r.validFrom()), local(r.validTo()))).toList();

package com.kartwala.prices;

import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional;
import org.springframework.web.server.ResponseStatusException;

import java.time.Clock;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.time.LocalDateTime;
import java.time.OffsetDateTime;
import java.time.ZoneId;
import java.time.ZoneOffset;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Optional;

/** Dated prices: a new price never overwrites; it takes its stretch of time, and the neighbours give way. */
@Service
class PriceSchedule {

    record Window(int pricePaise, OffsetDateTime from, OffsetDateTime to) {
    }

    record Schedule(long productId, List<Window> windows) {
    }

    record PriceAt(long productId, OffsetDateTime at, int pricePaise, OffsetDateTime validFrom, OffsetDateTime validTo) {
    }

    private record Row(long id, int pricePaise, Instant validFrom, Instant validTo) {
    }

    private final JdbcClient jdbc;
    private final Clock clock;
    private final ZoneId zone;

    PriceSchedule(JdbcClient jdbc, Clock clock, @Value("${shop.zone}") ZoneId zone) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.clock = clock;
        this.zone = zone;
    }

    /** The one price valid at that instant: valid_from <= at < valid_to. The exclusion constraint makes "one" true. */
    PriceAt priceAt(long productId, Instant at) {
        requireProduct(productId);
        return jdbc.sql("""
                        SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices
                        WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from <= ? AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > ?)""")
                .params(productId, utc(at), utc(at)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional()
                .map(r -> new PriceAt(productId, local(at), r.pricePaise(), local(r.validFrom()), local(r.validTo())))
                .orElseThrow(() -> new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "Product " + productId + " has no price at " + local(at)));
    }

    /**
     * Sets a price for [from, to) in shop time; to null means "from then on". Rows inside the window go, a row
     * covering its start is cut there, and a row covering its end continues after it.
     */
    @Transactional
    Schedule set(long productId, int pricePaise, LocalDateTime fromLocal, LocalDateTime toLocal) {
        Instant from = fromLocal.atZone(zone).toInstant();
        Instant to = toLocal == null ? null : toLocal.atZone(zone).toInstant();
        if (to != null && !to.isAfter(from)) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST, "The price must end after it starts");
        }
        if (from.isBefore(clock.instant())) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Prices in the past are history and cannot change");
        }
        // One schedule change per product at a time: a second one waits here, then sees the first one's rows.
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT id FROM products WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE").param(productId).query(Long.class).optional().isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No product " + productId);
        }
        Optional<Row> covering = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from < ? AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > ?)")
                .params(productId, utc(from), utc(from)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional();
        if (to == null) {
            jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ?").params(productId, utc(from)).update();
        } else {
            jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ? AND valid_to IS NOT NULL AND valid_to <= ?").params(productId, utc(from), utc(to)).update();
            jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_from = ? WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from >= ? AND valid_from < ?").params(utc(to), productId, utc(from), utc(to)).update();
        }
        covering.ifPresent(c -> {
            jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_to = ? WHERE id = ?").params(utc(from), c.id()).update();
            if (to != null && (c.validTo() == null || c.validTo().isAfter(to))) {   // the old price resumes after the new window
                insert(productId, c.pricePaise(), to, c.validTo());
            }
        });
        try {
            insert(productId, pricePaise, from, to);
        } catch (DataIntegrityViolationException e) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.CONFLICT, "The schedule changed meanwhile; read it and try again");
        }
        return schedule(productId);
    }

    /** Challenge 1. */
    Schedule fullSchedule(long productId) {
        requireProduct(productId);
        return schedule(productId);
    }

    /** Challenge 2: remove one future window; the window before it stretches over the gap, and equal neighbours merge. */
    @Transactional
    Schedule cancel(long productId, LocalDateTime fromLocal) {
        Instant from = fromLocal.atZone(zone).toInstant();
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT id FROM products WHERE id = ? FOR UPDATE").param(productId).query(Long.class).optional().isEmpty()) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No product " + productId);
        }
        Row window = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from = ?")
                .params(productId, utc(from)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No price starts at " + fromLocal));
        if (!window.validFrom().isAfter(clock.instant())) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.UNPROCESSABLE_CONTENT, "Prices in the past are history and cannot change");
        }
        jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE id = ?").param(window.id()).update();
        Optional<Row> before = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_to = ?")
                .params(productId, utc(from)).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional();
        Optional<Row> after = window.validTo() == null ? Optional.empty()
                : jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? AND valid_from = ?")
                        .params(productId, utc(window.validTo())).query(PriceSchedule::row).optional();
        before.ifPresent(b -> {
            if (after.isPresent() && after.get().pricePaise() == b.pricePaise()) {   // same price on both sides: one window
                jdbc.sql("DELETE FROM prices WHERE id = ?").param(after.get().id()).update();
                jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_to = ? WHERE id = ?").params(utc(after.get().validTo()), b.id()).update();
            } else {
                jdbc.sql("UPDATE prices SET valid_to = ? WHERE id = ?").params(utc(window.validTo()), b.id()).update();
            }
        });
        return schedule(productId);
    }

    Schedule schedule(long productId) {
        List<Window> windows = jdbc.sql("SELECT id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to FROM prices WHERE product_id = ? ORDER BY valid_from")
                .param(productId).query(PriceSchedule::row).list().stream()
                .map(r -> new Window(r.pricePaise(), local(r.validFrom()), local(r.validTo()))).toList();
        return new Schedule(productId, windows);
    }

    private void insert(long productId, int pricePaise, Instant from, Instant to) {
        jdbc.sql("INSERT INTO prices (product_id, price_paise, valid_from, valid_to) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)")
                .params(productId, pricePaise, utc(from), utc(to)).update();
    }

    private void requireProduct(long productId) {
        if (jdbc.sql("SELECT count(*) FROM products WHERE id = ?").param(productId).query(Long.class).single() == 0) {
            throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, "No product " + productId);
        }
    }

    private OffsetDateTime local(Instant instant) {
        return instant == null ? null : instant.atZone(zone).toOffsetDateTime();
    }

    /** Bound as an offset date-time, so PostgreSQL never interprets it in the server's or session's time zone. */
    private static OffsetDateTime utc(Instant instant) {
        return instant == null ? null : instant.atOffset(ZoneOffset.UTC);
    }

    private static Row row(java.sql.ResultSet rs, int i) throws java.sql.SQLException {
        OffsetDateTime to = rs.getObject("valid_to", OffsetDateTime.class);
        return new Row(rs.getLong("id"), rs.getInt("price_paise"), rs.getObject("valid_from", OffsetDateTime.class).toInstant(), to == null ? null : to.toInstant());
    }

Implementation approach

  1. Write the trap test: the zone-less, overlapping old table.
  2. Store dated prices as half-open timestamptz windows, with an exclusion constraint.
  3. Write the "as of" query, and convert local times at the edge, in the shop's zone.
  4. Fit new windows into the schedule inside one transaction, with the product row locked.

Design alternatives and trade-offs

ApproachWhat it costsVerdict
Dated windows + exclusion constraint + "as of" readsWrites must fit windows; reads are one indexed query.Chosen
Overwrite the price from a scheduled jobLate changes; history lost; a missed run is a wrong price.The trap
Dated rows with only a start ("from"), the latest start winsNo overlaps possible; ending a sale means inserting the old price again.Simpler, less expressive
A base price plus a separate promotions table with prioritiesClear for marketing; checkout must resolve priorities.For many overlapping offers
Times as timestamp plus a zone columnCorrect if every query applies the zone.Easy to get wrong

Database design

ObjectWhatWhy
prices_no_overlapEXCLUDE USING gist (product_id WITH =, tstzrange(valid_from, valid_to, '[)') WITH &&)One price per product at any instant; its GiST index can also serve the product lookup.
prices_window_orderCHECK valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > valid_fromNo empty or backwards windows.
prices_price_range, prices_product_fkCHECK and foreign keyNo impossible prices.
valid_from, valid_totimestamptzInstants, not wall-clock readings.

Transaction boundary: one schedule change, from locking the product row to the last insert.

CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS btree_gist;   -- lets a GiST exclusion constraint compare product_id with =

CREATE TABLE products (
    id   BIGINT       PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL
);

-- Every price a product has had or will have, each valid for a half-open stretch of time [valid_from, valid_to).
-- valid_to NULL means "until further notice". Nothing is overwritten, so "what did it cost at 21:04 yesterday" has an answer.
CREATE TABLE prices (
    id          BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id  BIGINT      NOT NULL CONSTRAINT prices_product_fk REFERENCES products (id),
    price_paise INTEGER     NOT NULL CONSTRAINT prices_price_range CHECK (price_paise BETWEEN 100 AND 10000000),
    valid_from  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    valid_to    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    CONSTRAINT prices_window_order CHECK (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > valid_from),
    -- At any instant, at most one price per product: checkout can never find two.
    CONSTRAINT prices_no_overlap EXCLUDE USING gist (product_id WITH =, tstzrange(valid_from, valid_to, '[)') WITH &&)
);

Interview takeaways

What is effective dating?

Storing each value with the period it is valid for, so the value at any instant (past, present or future) can be read without anything changing at that instant.

Why half-open windows?

Consecutive windows can share a boundary without overlapping, and each instant belongs to exactly one.

timestamp or timestamptz?

timestamptz for instants: it stores a moment; timestamp is a wall-clock reading with no zone, interpreted by whoever reads it.

How do you stop two prices applying at once?

An exclusion constraint on product and overlapping time range, so the database refuses the second, from any writer.

Where should time zones be handled?

At the edges: read the user's local time in their zone, store instants, and convert back for display.
